title: Bounded-precision section lifting over a henselian principal pair
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $t\in R$ be a non-zero-divisor, and assume $(R,tR)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $C$ be a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] on which multiplication by the image of $t$ is injective. Suppose $t^r\in H_{C/R}$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-per-gabber-ramero-obstruction-ideal]. Let $n>r$ and let $s_{n+r}:C/t^{n+r}C\to R/t^{n+r}R$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. There exists an $R$-algebra homomorphism $s:C\to R$ whose reduction modulo $t^n$ is the reduction of $s_{n+r}$. No agreement modulo a higher power is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.3 (Gabber–Ramero), equivalently [GR, 5.4.13] with the auxiliary ideal zero; a section is written contravariantly as an algebra map. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED; no Stacks tag for this specialized assertion.

proof.text: Choose a presentation $C=P/J$, $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, with $J$ finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By [def-per-gabber-ramero-obstruction-ideal], membership $t^r\in H_{C/R}\subseteq H_P$ supplies $h$ with $h\delta=t^r\operatorname{id}_{J/J^2}$. Choose representatives $a_{0,i}\in R$ of $s_{n+r}(x_i)$. Then $f(a_0)\in t^{n+r}R$ for every $f\in J$.

Set $q_0=n+r$ and $q_{k+1}=2(q_k-r)$. Inductively apply [lem-per-gabber-ramero-improve-precision] to choose $a_{k+1}\in R^d$ such that $f(a_{k+1})\in t^{q_{k+1}}R$ for all $f\in J$ and $a_{k+1}-a_k\in(t^{q_k-r}R)^d$. The base is Step 1. The formula $q_k=2r+2^k(n-r)$ follows by induction, so every $q_k>2r$, as required for each application. Both $q_k$ and $q_k-r$ tend to infinity, and $q_k-r\geq n$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.8 and Claim 5.4.14 in the proof of Proposition 5.4.13; explicit recurrence

proof.text: In $\widehat R=\varprojlim_mR/t^mR$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], define $\widehat a_i$ by its $m$-th residue, the eventually constant value of $a_{k,i}\bmod t^m$. This is well-defined: once $q_k-r\geq m$, every later difference lies in $t^mR$. These residues are compatible under reduction. For $f\in J$ and any $m$, choose $k$ with $q_k\geq m$ and $q_k-r\geq m$; coordinatewise evaluation gives $f(\widehat a)\bmod t^m=f(a_k)\bmod t^m=0$. Thus evaluation factors through $C=P/J$ to give $\widehat s:C\to\widehat R$. Since every difference is in $t^nR$, its $n$-th coordinate is exactly the reduction of $s_{n+r}$.

By [lem-per-gabber-ramero-ideal-calculus], the nonsmooth locus of $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $V(H_{C/R})$. A prime not containing $t$ cannot contain $H_{C/R}$, since $t^r\in H_{C/R}$. Hence this morphism is smooth on $\operatorname{Spec}C\setminus V(tC)$. Apply [lem-per-elkik-generic-smooth-section-approximation] to $(R,tR)$, $C$, $\widehat s$ and $N=n$. Its hypotheses are precisely Noetherianity, henselianity, finite presentation and this smoothness. It gives $s:C\to R$ whose reduction modulo $t^n$ is the $n$-th coordinate of $\widehat s$, which is the required reduction of $s_{n+r}$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2(ii), Lemma 5.4.12 and proof of Proposition 5.4.13

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.4.13 (Noetherian case): Lemma 5.4.8 iteration followed by Lemma 5.4.12. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Explicit quotient-coordinate assembly.
